editorial.headline: Jewellery Retail Is Nationally Open—But Closed to PMA Registration in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This retail activity permits full foreign ownership nationally, yet Bali’s permanent risk-based moratorium blocks its PMA registration on the island.
editorial.body:
At the national level, this is an open foreign-investment retail activity, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. Its territory is jewellery retail: the sale of goods made from precious stones, diamonds, diamond powder, gemstones, imitation gemstones, precious metals and non-precious metals. The description is broad in the articles it captures—rings, necklaces, bracelets, earrings, hairpins, brooches, belts and precious-metal buttons are all expressly included—while remaining precise about the commercial act: retail trade in jewellery goods.

The range of materials is equally deliberate. It embraces jewellery made with platinum, gold and silver, as well as pieces involving gemstones or their imitations, without reducing the activity to one material or one form of adornment. The registration is open at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scale. That means the stated activity can be registered across all four listed business scales; the scope remains the retail sale of the jewellery goods described, rather than being confined to a single size of enterprise.

In Bali, however, the national rule is not the end of the inquiry. A PMA investor cannot register this activity in Bali today: its Bali position is blocked at the risk-class level. The record places the OSS risk assessment for the Besar scale at Low or Medium-Low across every scope. That brings the activity within Bali’s island-wide, permanent moratorium on PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activity. The Bali result is a registration block, not a different national ownership percentage.

The distinction is clean, but consequential. Nationally, foreign ownership may reach 100%, within the stated retail scope and across the four listed scales. In Bali, PMA registration is unavailable because the risk classification triggers the provincial moratorium. These are not competing readings to be averaged into a softer answer: they are two geographic layers of the same decision. The national ceiling remains national; for a PMA registration on the island, the Bali block is decisive.
